items.title: Diesel shortages: Why the global economy has more to fear than rising petrol prices
items.excerpt: Key Points: Diesel is the backbone of global transport, agriculture and industrial activity, making it far more important to the broader economy than petrol. Middle East supply disruptions and reduced Russian exports have tightened an already vulnerable market for refined products. Limited refining capacity and depleted inventories make it difficult to respond quickly to supply shortages. Persistently high diesel prices pose a significant inflation and growth risk, even if crude oil prices begin to ease. Why diesel matters more than petrol While rising petrol prices mainly affect motorists, diesel plays a much broader and more critical role in the global economy. items.title: Canadian Dollar futures hit 18-month low on weak jobs report.
items.excerpt: Canadian Dollar futures fell to an 18-month low as unexpected job losses in Canada weighed on market sentiment. Statistics Canada reported September employment dropped by 68,300, defying expectations for a gain of 9,200, while the unemployment rate climbed to 6.5%. Labor force participation declined to 64.8%, its lowest level since 1997 outside of the pandemic. The weak labor market data pushed back Bank of Canada rate hike expectations, with money markets pricing out an October rate increase. Meanwhile, CME Group's FedWatch Tool indicates higher probability for a December FOMC rate hike in the U.S., creating a divergence in monetary policy outlooks that continues to exert downward pressure on the Canadian dollar.

items.title: US midterms: Scenarios, and what they can mean for AI and bond yields
items.excerpt: Key points: Gridlock could be the most market-friendly outcome. A divided Congress may limit further fiscal expansion, potentially easing pressure on bond yields and supporting equity valuations. AI faces political risks, but the bigger challenge is financing. Election outcomes could influence data-centre approvals and energy policy, but rising power costs, debt and pressure to deliver returns may matter more for AI's next phase. A Republican win could favour AI infrastructure, but pressure bonds. Policy continuity may support AI, energy and financials, but concerns over deficits and higher yields could offset the benefits for equity valuations. items.title: Japanese Yen futures held range as Euro tested 16-month lows.
items.excerpt: Dan Deming analyzes recent price action across the FX markets, highlighting relative strength in Japanese Yen futures as they trade higher for a second consecutive session. Despite the recent uptick, the yen remains in a tight weekly range as markets digest hawkish Fed minutes and strong demand from recent 10-Year and 30-Year Treasury auctions. Deming discusses how these well-received Treasury auctions are influencing the U.S. dollar pricing structure and impacting broader currency markets. In addition, Deming breaks down the recent weakness in Euro FX futures, which recently pushed down to a 16-month low before bouncing slightly in today's session. Finally, he notes similar recent weakness in British Pound and Australian Dollar futures amidst a broadly muted day for foreign exchange.
